newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end at highs after Dow firms.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end at highs after Dow firms.

text.p: SPI 2411 +18 US 30yr cl 6.58 unch
10yrbond futs 92.480 +0.005 Gold NY 368.85 Lon fix 368.90
*Stocks ended near their highs on light volume after the Dow posted modest gains in a thin market. Volume 134.7 million, Value A$434.5 million, 768 shares traded, 237 steady, 367 rises, 164 falls
Australian shares closed at their highs in thin trade on Friday after the Dow posted two straight gains. The local market resumed trade after being closed on the Christmas and Boxing Day holidays.
The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index ended 14.2 points up at 2,395.6, its high for the session.
The December share price index finished up 18 points at 2,411 and at a 15.4 point premium to the underlying index.
Dealers said few investors took advantage of the stronger sentiment with most fund managers absent from the market after the Christmas break and ahead of the weekend.

A late surge of buying was enough to push the All Ordinaries index to a record closing high, the market eclipsing its previous record of 2,392.7 set on November 20. The market's all-time high of 2,408.9 was set on November 26.
"The market fed on itself this afternoon with the few investors around deciding they did not want to miss out on an end of year rally," a Sydney-based dealer said.
The dealer said the late squeeze was exacerbated by thinness of the market and the reasonable possibility of end of second quarter window dressing by institutions next Tuesday.

Benefiting most from the market's rise were bellwether resource issues BHP and WMC while favoured industrial stocks included finance and property group Lend Lease Corp and beverage company Coca-Cola Amatil.
Dealers said Coca-Cola Amatil stock continued to recover from heavy selling in the past month and a half after it surprised the market with an earnings downgrade in mid-November.
Major banks finished the session mixed with Westpac and National Australia bank closing weaker after both recently paid final dividends.
In other markets, Australian bonds closed little changed from their pre-Christmas levels as they again waited for inspiration from the U.S with November U.S. durable goods orders due later today.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds finished at 7.44 percent, unchanged from its close on Tuesday.
The Australian dollar drifted higher through a very subdued Friday session but was still down on the levels seen before the local holiday.
At 4.45 (0545 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7962/67.

Bellwether resource issues ended at their highs after finding good buying support in thin market after two stronger sessions from Wall Street while the Australian market was closed for the Christmas break.
Beverage group's shares continued to recover after being sold heavily after an earnings downgrade in mid-November.
Gold producer's shares rose strongly on thin volume after the company revealed that South African mining house JCI Ltd had acquired a direct 8.51 percent stake in the company.
The company said the Gobe joint venture received the necessary licences to commence development of the Gobe oil field in PNG.
-- Michael Stapleton, Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
